findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee turn off the faucet without using a barrier. CORRECTED: Employee was educated on using the paper towel as a barrier, and rewashed their hands, this time using a paper towel as a barrier when turning off the faucet handle. Ensure that a barrier is used to run off the faucet to avoid recontaminating clean hands after handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed the inside top of the microwave has an accumulation of food debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food debris. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and an employee cleaned the microwave, and updated cleaning procedures to include the inside top of the microwave. Ensure that the inside of the microwave to clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee filled a sanitizer bucket and then proceeded to put on gloves to handle food without washing hands in-between. The employee was instructed to hand wash when the action was observed. The employee and PIC were educated that hands must be washed after filling up sanitizer buckets (and after other sources of contamination) and before donning gloves. Ensure than foods employees always wash hands properly.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the sugar scoop was stored with the handle in-contact with the sugar. The employee working was notified and the scoop was removed from the container. The inspector suggests storing the scoop on top of the container. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are stored with the handle not in-contact with the food to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(B) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(B) In food that is not time/temperature control for safety food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. The employee working was informed and they made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. The employee and PIC were reminded that a sanitizer bucket must be available whenever food preparation is occurring. They were also reminded that wet wiping cloths must be stored in the sanitizer bucket between uses. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. A barrier must be used to operate faucet handles to prevent recontamination of clean hands. The PIC was asked to educated their staff about the proper handwashing procedure.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket made when inspector arrived (at this time, an employee was prepping sandwiches for lunch). The PIC created a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that during all hours of operation there is chemical sanitizer available. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed that was not cove base under the oven. The PIC stated that it had been removed during a repair and had not been re-attached yet. An employee re-attached cove base to this area during the inspection. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Cindy, Rachel and Stephany need to renew their CFM certificates, will call CK to figure out when they can do that. Received letter from CK regarding CFM certificates.  

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the counter top. No sanitizer had been made except the sanitizer in the triple sink. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution when not directly being used for wiping surfaces. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer in the future. The cloth was removed and placed in a new sanitizer bucket. Corrected on site. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: On arrival, no sanitizer bucket was prepared. Inspector observed there to be sanitizer in the triple sink, but a sanitizer bucket must be made up for wiping surfaces if approved sanitizer is not used with paper towels and spray. Ensure that during all operations, sanitizer buckets are available for sanitizing surfaces in the facility. A sanitizer bucket was made during the inspection with appropriate 200 ppm quaternary ammonia concentration. Corrected on site.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the caulking on the hand sink and triple sink had begun to deteriorate. These surfaces are subject to moisture. Ensure that they are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Re-caulking has already begun and will be completed by the end of the day. Ensure that re-caulking is completed by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Fridge next to the oven observed to be ~50F. Fridge is intended to be used for nonperishable items only, though non-dairy milks and yogurts observed to be in the cooler. CORRECTED-- Non-dairy items moved to the milk cooler. PIC is considering replacing the cooler.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed R-I Cooler to be out of temperature. Cooler is next to oven. Air temperature was measured to be 46F. Cooler was out of temperature for unknown amount of time. PIC stated longest item in fridge was jelly. Jelly was probed to be 48F. Corrected. All TCS foods were voluntarily discarded from R-I Cooler. This included 2 containers of cream cheese (16oz), 12 containers of yogurt(27lbs), and 2 bottles of ranch (44fl oz). All other foods will be moved to other cooler. Cooler was turned down.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed spatula utensil to be soiled with physical debris. All food contact surfaces must be washed, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent contamination. 

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed microwave to be soiled with debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned as necessasry to prevent build-up. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510(a) Observed a food employee switch from handling soiled dishware to handling clean, sanitized dishware without properly washing their hands. Food employees shall wash their hands any time they may have become contaminated to prevent potential contamination of food or food contact surfaces. Proper hand washing was discussed. All food employees responsible for ware washing shall be knowledgeable on how to prevent potential contamination of clean, sanitized dishware.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-820(d) Observed the third basin of the three compartment sink to have 0 ppm QT. Facility management states that sanitizer dispenser was serviced approximately two weeks ago by MJ Kellner. Facility management contacted MJ Kellner and they arrived to service the chemical dispenser during the inspection. MJ Kellner discovered a clog in the sanitizer line. Once clog was removed, sanitizer in the third basin was tested and had a concentration of 200 ppm. All food employees responsible for ware washing shall be knowledgeable in proper practices including testing for appropriate concentration, contact time, and how to prevent potential contamination of clean, sanitized food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer in the reach in cooler in the dry storage area. Kitchen staff stated that the unit had recently been cleaned and the thermometer was most likely misplaced. Provide a thermometer for this unit.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed a box of Frito Lay chips stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Food and single service items should be stored at least six inches from the gruond. Kitchen staff moved the box to a shelving unit to CORRECT the violation.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed plastic plates stored with food contact surface exposed. Kitchen staff member inverted the plates to CORRECT the violation. Single service items should be stored in a manner that protects food contact surfaces from contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: Observed a spray bottle of sanitizer stored in a milk crate with single service items (Styrofoam cups). Spray bottle was removed by kitchen staff to CORRECT the violation. Toxic substances should be stored away from food and single service items.750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed several spray bottles in the dry storage area and one bottle above the three compartment sink to be unlabeled. Kitchen staff provided labels for all toxic substances during the inspection to CORRECT the violation. Label all bottles of toxic substances. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
